profile.campus: Microsoft Potranco Road/FM 1957 campus near Castroville, Medina County, TX (SAT80, SAT81, SAT82, one site, distinct from the separate TRP3/SAT46 site about 4.3 miles away)
profile.address: 18844 FM 1957, Castroville area, Medina County, Texas 78009
profile.reading:
This building sits at 18844 FM 1957 near Castroville, Texas, about 27 miles west of downtown San Antonio, on a rural Medina County site that trade publication CoStar has identified as home to Microsoft's SAT80, SAT81, and SAT82 data center buildings together. CoStar reported in 2024 that Microsoft filed a Texas work permit that week for a $482.6 million, single level, 244,676 square foot data center building at this address under the project name SAT82, designed by WSP USA Inc., with construction expected to run from April 2026 to early 2028. That same CoStar report described SAT80 and SAT81 as standing at the same address under a separate, previously announced investment of more than $230 million, a figure that matches a Medina County Microsoft project the San Antonio Current separately reported without naming a specific SAT code. CoStar characterized all three buildings as colocation data centers built to rent capacity to third party tenant companies rather than exclusively hosting Microsoft's own cloud workloads, a characterization this registry repeats as CoStar's own framing rather than something Microsoft itself has confirmed publicly.

The San Antonio Report has separately described what it called the SAT80-1 and SAT80-2 buildings at this same rural site as each exceeding 106,000 square feet on a shared 206 acre parcel, reporting that framing before CoStar's later account of the SAT82 expansion, so this registry cannot confirm whether the San Antonio Report's SAT80-1 and SAT80-2 labels map directly onto the SAT80 and SAT81 buildings this registry tracks or describe an earlier two building phase that SAT82 later joined. Microsoft has built at least eight data centers across the San Antonio region, spanning Bexar and Medina counties, since first opening two facilities there in 2015 at roughly $90 million each, with cumulative regional investment exceeding $1.2 billion as of August 2023. San Antonio's city council approved a 15 year Chapter 380 tax reimbursement in 2013 covering 40 percent of property taxes in exchange for a $250 million Microsoft investment commitment and 20 new jobs, and Microsoft's continued expansion into rural Medina County reflects the same pattern of steadily broadening its footprint well beyond that original commitment.

CPS Energy, San Antonio's municipally owned electric and gas utility, supplies power to this site and has cited large commercial and industrial customers, data centers among them, in its own integrated resource planning as it weighs new generation for growing demand. Because CPS Energy is municipally owned rather than investor owned, large load agreements with customers like Microsoft are negotiated directly with the city owned utility rather than through the Public Utility Commission of Texas process governing most of the state's investor owned utilities. No total campus megawatt figure for this site was found in sourcing reviewed this session.

reading.body:
SAT82 is a single-level data center building of 244,676 square feet now under construction on a rural Medina County site about 27 miles west of San Antonio. It is one of three buildings on a shared 206-acre campus, joined by SAT80 and SAT81, each over 106,000 square feet, under a combined investment exceeding $712 million. Microsoft filed a work permit in July 2024 for SAT82's $482.6 million build, with construction scheduled to run from April 2026 to early 2028. No individual building or campus power figure has been published by Microsoft or located in available sources.

The campus is characterized by trade press as purpose-built colocation infrastructure designed to rent capacity to third-party tenants rather than exclusively hosting Microsoft's own workloads, though Microsoft has not publicly confirmed this framing. Power is supplied by CPS Energy, San Antonio's municipally owned utility, under a negotiated large load agreement outside the standard regulatory process used elsewhere in Texas. The site is one of at least eight data centers Microsoft has built in the San Antonio region since 2015, reflecting expansion well beyond the 2013 tax incentive deal that originally committed the company to a $250 million investment and 20 jobs.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities; only 19 publish power specifications totaling 475 megawatts. This campus is not among those 19 published figures and therefore cannot be ranked by power capacity. Its contribution to regional and state AI infrastructure capacity remains unknown. Without a published power specification, its significance to grid constraints and compute scaling cannot be assessed from available data.
